title: Updating an Old Electrical System: From BX to NM in a Historic Home
summary: This This Old House episode documents a retrofit of an older home’s electrical system. The hosts discover armored BX cable throughout the house and place the work in historical context, noting that the structure likely dates from the late 19th to early 20th century and that knob-and-tube wiring would have been expected in some periods but is not present. They explain key wiring generations: knob-and-tube (single-conductor, routed through studs with knobs and tubes), BX/armored cable (two conductors in one jacket with external protection), and modern NM cable (nonmetallic sheathed, two conductors plus ground). The discussion highlights practical differences, including ease of installation, pull-through capability, and color-coding (yellow jacket indicating 20-amp NM). The plan shown is to remove the armored shield and replace it with NM cable, emphasizing straightforward installation and preparation for temporary power during the upgrade. The segment also touches on expected timelines for completing the work and the approach to providing temporary power as work progresses.
